title: AssetInventory
description: Claude's B-DISCOVER output: real discovered visual assets plus block-level coverage planning against script_manifest.json. Central rule: DISCOVERY IS NOT VERIFICATION -- finding a plausible search result is not the same as having looked at the thing. Coverage is block-centric: block_coverage[].target_visual_sec is the corresponding block's MEASURED duration_sec from tts_manifest.json (never an estimate) -- there is no outline/beat intermediary in this pipeline. A single long source video may contain multiple non-contiguous useful regions; each is its own usable_segments[] entry rather than one start/end pair per asset. See agents/agent_b_archive_visual_editor.md.

status.description: pending: B-DISCOVER has not run. gathered: every script_manifest.json block has exactly one block_coverage entry, none is critical_gap, and overall_effective_coverage (see agents/agent_b_archive_visual_editor.md) is >= 0.90. approved: reviewed. B-EDIT is gated on this reaching gathered or approved.

environment_limitations.description: Capabilities this run genuinely lacked, stated plainly rather than hidden -- e.g. 'cannot decode video frames, so no video asset can exceed verification_method: metadata_only', or 'domain X blocks this crawler'. A limitation recorded here is the justification for weaker verification_method values elsewhere in the file.

assets.description: Every real asset discovered, regardless of which block(s) use it. The same asset may be allocated to multiple blocks via block_coverage[].allocations -- store it once here. Downloading the source file never trims or overwrites it: usable_segments records permitted RANGES within the intact original, it does not cut it.

source_url.description: Where the asset lives. At least one of source_url or local_path must be present (enforced above) -- an asset with neither is not a discovered asset. Prefer having both once downloaded.

source_title.description: Title of the page, archive record, or publication the asset came from -- so a later reviewer can retrace the find

asset_type.description: There is exactly ONE video type. 'Contextual' is not a media type -- it is expressed via an allocation's relevance: contextual instead (see block_coverage[].allocations[].relevance). A contextual video is still asset_type: video.

description.description: What the asset actually shows. If verification_method is not visually_inspected, this describes what the SOURCE CLAIMS it shows -- say so.

exact_subject_match.description: Whether this asset genuinely shows the exact subject requested. MUST NOT be set true unless verification_method is visually_inspected. A title, filename, caption, search snippet, or metadata field is never sufficient evidence that an image or video depicts a specific model year or variant. Any allocation using this asset with relevance: exact requires this to be true.

access_status.description: How much of the source was actually reached.

verification_method.description: How the asset's CONTENT was established. visually_inspected: the image, or the relevant video frames, were actually viewed (e.g. via scripts/media_probe.py's contact sheets). metadata_only: title/caption/EXIF/archive record read, content not viewed. search_result_only: known only from a search listing. unverified: neither content nor metadata confirmed. usable_segments may only be non-empty when this is visually_inspected.

duration_sec.description: Video only (required when asset_type is video). Total source duration, e.g. from scripts/media_probe.py's probe(). Used to bound usable_segments -- a segment's end_sec must not exceed this.

usable_segments.description: Video only. A source video may contain several useful, non-contiguous regions -- one entry per region, rather than a single asset-wide start/end. Only allowed when verification_method is visually_inspected; empty or absent otherwise. Never invent timestamps from a title, description, or search result.

segment_id.description: Unique across the ENTIRE asset_inventory.json (not just within this asset), e.g. 'asset_014_s1'. Referenced by block_coverage[].allocations[].segment_id and later by edit_plan.json clips.

end_sec.description: Must exceed start_sec, and must not exceed the asset's duration_sec when known.

visual_quality.description: Use unknown unless the asset was actually viewed

license.description: Licence/rights status if known, or an explicit note that it is unknown

reusable.description: Whether this asset (or its segments) is generic/flexible enough to reasonably allocate to more than one block (e.g. a contextual factory shot or a period logo), as opposed to something that only makes sense for the one block it was found for. See asset_library/ for cross-episode reuse.

block_coverage.description: PRIMARY coverage contract. Exactly one entry per block in script_manifest.json's blocks array -- a block with no entry, or more than one entry, is an error. target_visual_sec must equal that block's measured duration_sec from tts_manifest.json.

target_visual_sec.description: The visual workload budget for this block. MUST equal tts_manifest.json's measured duration_sec for this block_id -- there is no estimate to fall back to in this pipeline; TTS must be measured before this is meaningful.

planned_visual_sec.description: MUST equal the sum of this entry's allocations[].planned_sec (within rounding tolerance) -- not a number claimed independently of the allocations that back it.

coverage_ratio.description: planned_visual_sec / target_visual_sec. Deterministic -- must equal that division (within rounding). If target_visual_sec is 0, set this to 1.0 and explain in notes.

coverage_status.description: V0 planning thresholds against coverage_ratio: sufficient >= 0.90, partial >= 0.60 and < 0.90, critical_gap < 0.60. Simple planning guidance, not a scoring system. Per-block status alone does not open the B-EDIT gate -- see agents/agent_b_archive_visual_editor.md for the episode-level overall_effective_coverage requirement.

allocations.description: Assets (and, for video, specific usable_segments) planned for this block's screen time. May be empty only if coverage_status is critical_gap.

asset_id.description: References an asset_id in this file's assets array. The same asset_id may appear in multiple blocks' allocations.

segment_id.description: Video assets only, and required for them: references one of that asset's usable_segments[].segment_id. Absent for photo/document/etc. assets, which have no segments. Different segments of the same video asset may serve different blocks -- that's expected, not a problem.

planned_sec.description: Approximate planned screen time for this asset within this block. For a video allocation this must not exceed the referenced segment's own duration (end_sec - start_sec) -- only the selected usable material counts, never the source video's full runtime. Soft editorial guidance (not a hard validation limit) for typical values: ~15-35s for a good relevant video segment, ~8-18s photo, ~10-20s brochure/document/magazine, ~8-15s map/chart. Longer is fine when genuinely appropriate -- don't mechanically chop a strong clip just to fit a range.

relevance.description: exact: the exact vehicle/object/event being discussed -- requires the referenced asset's exact_subject_match to be true. adjacent: a closely related model, sibling vehicle, factory, company, component, or same project. contextual: period/geography/industry footage supporting the narration without claiming to depict the exact subject (this is how a 'contextual video' is expressed -- asset_type stays video, relevance carries the contextuality). documentary_fallback: brochure, document, advertisement, magazine scan, map, chart, archive still, etc. A block is not required to have exact-relevance material for every second -- a coherent visual story matters more than exactness for every allocation.
